question: What is meant by closed test setting?

extractive_spans: closed test limits all the data for learning should not be beyond the given training set, while open test does not take this limitation
evidence: External data and pre-trained embedding. Whereas both encoder and graph model are about exploring a way to get better performance only by improving the model strength itself. title: Attention Is All You Need for Chinese Word Segmentation
answer_short: closed test limits all the data for learning should not be beyond the given training set
answer_rationale: The definition of closed test setting is explicitly provided in Text 4, Section 9, which states that 'closed test limits all the data for learning should not be beyond the given training set'. This is further corroborated by Text 1, Section 58, which mentions that using unsupervised segmentation features derived from the training dataset does not violate the rule of closed test of SIGHAN Bakeoff.
